Maya (encops): Heads-up — vulnerability scanner flagged a few DB snapshots in the internal backup bucket that are missing SSE-CMK metadata. Looks like upload path skipped the CMK tag. Can we confirm scope?
Jon (sre): Oof, which bucket & snapshot ids?
Maya (encops): bucket: s3://redwood-prod-db-backups region: us-east-1. Example object: `snap-2026-03-18-17-34.tar.gz` — found via `aws s3api head-object`.
Priya (db): I pulled the list — about 6 objects from last 48h, all from the legacy backup-agent job running on db-mgmt-2. Likely the agent used old creds after the recent service-account rotation.
Eli (infra): That job should be using the `backup-uploader` IAM role with CMK grants attached. If creds rolled without reattaching grants, uploads can succeed but without `x-amz-server-side-encryption` headers.
Maya (encops): Timeline: scanner first alerted at ~4601239600. Confirmed unencrypted metadata at 4601239722. No evidence of public exposure.
Jon (sre): Low-level triage: any restores possible? Is the object actually plaintext or SSE-S3?
Priya (db): `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-prod-db-backups --key snap-2026-03-18-17-34.tar.gz`
Priya (db): returned `{"ServerSideEncryption": null, "SSEKMSKeyId": null}` — so it was uploaded without SSE.
Eli (infra): OK. Root cause hypothesis: after the KMS provider key alias rotation last week, we rotated the CMK but forgot to re-lend the `Grant` to the `backup-uploader` role for the new alias. Upload still permitted via IAM putObject but missing encryption header.
Maya (encops): Immediate mitigations?
Jon (sre): 1) Revoke any stale creds for the backup-agent host. 2) Block further uploads to that prefix via a temporary bucket policy that denies PutObject without `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header. 3) Re-run scan for unencrypted objects and quarantine.
Eli (infra): I'll push the deny policy now. Patch snippet:
```
{
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Action": "s3:PutObject",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-db-backups/*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"}
  }
}
```
Priya (db): For remediation on the existing objects, options: re-upload encrypted copy, or apply S3 object copy with encryption using the CMK, e.g.:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-db-backups/snap-2026-03-18-17-34.tar.gz \
  s3://redwood-prod-db-backups/snap-2026-03-18-17-34.tar.gz \
  --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/redwood-prod-backups
```
Maya (encops): Note: copying client-side will create a new PUT — ensure KMS grants available for the actor doing the copy. For large objects we should avoid double egress. Consider server-side copy (`aws s3api copy-object`) which can be in-region and uses S3 internal copy with SSE-KMS header.
Jon (sre): Also need audit log trail: which principal performed the upload? Check CloudTrail events for `PutObject` on those keys between 4601238000–4601239800.
Maya (encops): I pulled one event: `userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName: backup-agent-sa`, `sourceIPAddress`: 10.12.5.18, `eventTime`: 2026-03-18T17:34:12Z.
Eli (infra): That host had a rotated kube secret. Looks like the secret update failed to include the new KMS grant ARN. We'll need an RBAC+grant checklist for the next rotation.
Priya (db): Action items from DB team: 1) Prevent restore from those snapshots until we mark them remediated. 2) If we re-encrypt via copy, tag snapshot metadata `reencrypted_by=encops` and `incident=4601239876`.
Maya (encops): Security action items: 1) Add automated rule to fail backup job when PutObject doesn't return SSE headers. 2) Add audit alert for any PutObject with `ServerSideEncryption` null. 3) Temp mitigate with bucket deny (Jon/Eli doing).
Jon (sre): I'll add an oncall runbook step: `detect-unencrypted-backup` that runs list+head-object and opens paged ticket if >0.
Eli (infra): I'll re-issue the CMK grant to `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader` and confirm with `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-prod-backups`.
Maya (encops): Note about KMS grants and restore windows: long-running restores may need `GrantToken` during rotation. Make sure the grant includes `RetireGrant` permission not just `Decrypt`.
Priya (db): Quick vuln-triage: Are these objects accessible by any service account that shouldn't have them? They live in a prod bucket with restricted ACLs; no public access. Scoping risk: moderate (data sensitivity), likelihood: low (no external access).
Maya (encops): Incident classification: security-corrective (no evidence of exfil). We'll track as SEV-low and close after remediation + postmortem.
Jon (sre): ETA for blocking policy: 10m. ETA for grant reattach: 30m. ETA for object re-encryption (6 files ~2TB): we'll schedule server-side copy during off-peak, estimate 3 hours.
Eli (infra): Grant reattached. Confirmed with `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-prod-backups` — output includes `GranteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader`.
encops-bot: Noted incident 4601239876 created in tracker and assigned to Maya, Jon, Priya.
Priya (db): Starting server-side copy job now — will tag objects on completion.
Maya (encops): Postmortem items: - add grant checklist on KMS rotations - add CI job that verifies backup-agent uploads include SSE headers - update RBAC runbook to include secret rotation validation for KMS grants - daily audit query for `ServerSideEncryption` null objects.
Jon (sre): I'll open the postmortem doc and link it to the incident.
Priya (db): Copy job finished. All 6 objects show `ServerSideEncryption: aws:kms` now. Tags added.
Maya (encops): Closing timeline: detection -> mitigation -> remediation done in ~3.5h. Leaving follow-up tasks in the PM. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Jon (sre): +1. Let's add a canary backup job to validate headers too.
Eli (infra): Created follow-up infra ticket to add grant validation in the secret rotation playbook.
Maya (encops): Marking thread resolved. If anything else pops up ping here or escalate to encops oncall.
